headline: Sosa's 3-RBI game lifts Phillies past Cardinals, 6-5
recap: The Phillies beat the Cardinals 6-5 in St. Louis on Monday, taking a 4-2 lead through seven innings, adding two more runs in the eighth, then holding on as the Cardinals answered with three runs in the bottom of that inning. Edmundo Sosa drove in three runs on a 2-for-3 night with a double, and Kyle Schwarber went 2-for-3 with a double and an RBI. Andrew Painter earned the win with 5.1 innings and two runs allowed, Alan Rangel worked 2.2 innings in relief and picked up the hold despite allowing three runs, and Jonathan Bowlan closed it out with a scoreless ninth for his first save.
The win was Philadelphia's second straight, moving the team to 64-56 and second place in the NL East, 7.5 games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves.

The Phillies continue their series in St. Louis tonight, with Cristopher Sanchez starting opposite the Cardinals' Andre Pallante; first pitch is scheduled for 7:46 PM ET at Busch Stadium. DraftKings has Philadelphia as a -162 favorite on the moneyline.
